text:
maria: Heads-up, seeing big east-west latency spikes for GPU pods in i-clus-3 starting ~10:22 UTC. RDMA QPs resetting, high packet loss. Anyone else?

sam: Yup, noticed the same. Captured a quick pcap — looks like IPv6 neighbor adverts flipping between two MACs for the same /128. RDMA flows drop after the flip.

sam: ```
# ip -6 neigh show dev eth0 | grep 2607:xxxx::a
2607:xxxx::a dev eth0 lladdr 0a:1b:2c:3d:4e:5f REACHABLE
# later
2607:xxxx::a dev eth0 lladdr 0a:1b:2c:3d:4e:60 STALE
```

ops-bot: :bell: Incident created: INC-2337 - "v6 advert oscillation -> rdma QP resets" (assigned: eng-infra)

lee: Can you paste `ip -6 route show` and `sysctl net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_redirects` from the affected node(s)? Also check `ip -s -s neigh` counts.

maria: Pasting quick extracts:

```
# sysctl net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_redirects
net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_redirects = 1
# ip -6 route show dev eth0
2607:xxxx::/64 proto kernel metric 256 pref medium  src 2607:xxxx::a
::/0 via fe80::beef dev eth0  metric 1024
```

maria: `ip -s -s neigh` shows a lot of NUD_FAILED/STALE entries for the same addr across nodes.

julia: Observed conntrack skew too — many conntrack entries still bound to the old MAC after the ND mapping flipped, so replies were being hashed to a stale path and dropped. Kernel wasn't recycling those flows fast enough.

anand: This matches a known kernel interaction where duplicate RAs from two paths cause neighbor table flaps and conntrack associations to persist incorrectly (seen on older 6.x kernels). Could be fabric doing an ECMP rewrite during maintenance. Workarounds:

```
# immediate mitigation steps (run on affected compute nodes)
ip -s -s neigh flush all
systemctl restart rdma.service || restart hoisted RDMA daemon
# disable accept_redirects until fix is deployed
sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_redirects=0
# optionally reduce neigh GC timeouts
sysctl -w net.ipv6.neigh.default.gc_stale_time=30
```

sam: After flushing neigh and restarting RDMA on node-7, QPs recovered and p50/p99 latency returned to baseline. Temporary mitigation worked.

lee: Thanks. We should: 1) push a transient sysctl change (accept_redirects=0) via kured/daemonset to compute nodes in i-clus-3, 2) add an alert that triggers when the same IPv6 address appears with >1 distinct lladdr within 60s across the cluster, and 3) open an upstream kernel bug ticket linking our traces. I'll file infra TCK-4029.

maria: Filed TCK-4029 with packet captures and conntrack dumps attached. Leaving accept_redirects off for now in i-clus-3. Monitoring. :eyes:

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: INC-2337 status changed to INVESTIGATING (assignee: lee)

julia: Also adding a health-check into the RDMA smoke test that validates return-path stability for IPv6 peers; will open a PR in perf-tests.

anand: Long term: vendor fabric team to check for RA/ND duplication during ECMP churn and we should track kernel backports.

maria: Thanks all — keeping this thread for postmortem notes. Will follow up with timeline once monitoring stabilizes. :thumbsup:
